headline: Coevolution and comparative genomics infer microbial interaction and symbiosis networks
label: Network Inference Across Biological Systems
summary: Genome-scale coevolution and comparative genomics now recover interaction structure from indirect relational evidence across microbial and symbiotic systems.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of relational structure from indirect genomic evidence rather than direct measurement of interactions. The siderophore study infers specific siderophore-receptor pairings from uncurated genomes via coevolution, reconstructing iron scavenging networks across nine bacterial taxa and revealing topological diversity in microbial exploitation. The lichen study is comparative rather than network-based: it analyzes 309 ascomycete genomes, 191 of them lichen symbionts, and links CAZyme repertoires to photobiont carbon subsidies. ECLIPSE embeds ESKAPE pan-proteomes in the Protein Universe Atlas sequence similarity network to find and rank dark proteins. What is new is the transfer of network-based reconstruction to genomic data spanning bacterial interaction, fungal symbiosis, and pathogen proteome scales. The items differ considerably in method, so this thread describes the dominant pattern rather than a feature shared by every item.
